question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

?, -570, -580, -590, -600, -610, -620, -630
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. -560.

GIVEN

• ?, -570, -580, -590, -600, -610, -620, -630

SOLUTION

• The series decreases by 10 at each step: -570, -580, -590 ... (each term is 10 less than the previous).

• So the first (missing) term must be 10 more than -570.

• -570 + 10 = -560.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Common difference is -10; move one step backward from -570 → add 10 → -560.

NOTE

• In a negative arithmetic progression, going backward (to the left) you ADD the common difference; going forward you subtract it.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

FZ, DX, BU, ZQ, XL, ?, TY, RQ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. VF.

GIVEN

• FZ, DX, BU, ZQ, XL, ?, TY, RQ

SOLUTION

• First letters: F(6), D(4), B(2), Z(26), X(24), ?, T(20), R(18) → decrease by 2 each time. After X(24) comes 24-2 = 22 = V.

• Second letters: Z(26), X(24), U(21), Q(17), L(12), ?, Y(25), Q(17) → differences are -2, -3, -4, -5, -6, ... So 12-6 = 6 = F (next -7 gives 6-7 = -1 → 25 = Y, then -8 → Q).

• Missing term = VF.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter: fixed gap -2; second letter: increasing gap -2,-3,-4,-5,-6...

NOTE

• When a difference goes below 1, wrap around by adding 26 (A=1 ... Z=26).

question:
Select the option that is related to the second letter cluster in the same way as the third letter cluster is related to the fourth letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

? : AQ :: UD : PW :: KO : FL
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. FJ.

GIVEN

• ? : AQ :: UD : PW :: KO : FL

SOLUTION

• First letter: U(21)→P(16) is -5; K(11)→F(6) is -5. So required first letter - 5 = A(1) → first letter = 1+5 = 6 = F.

• Second letter: D(4)→W(23) are opposite letters (4+23 = 27); O(15)→L(12) also add to 27. So second letter is the opposite of Q(17) → 27-17 = 10 = J.

• Missing cluster = FJ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Rule = (1st letter -5, 2nd letter → its A-Z opposite). Apply to AQ: A+5 = F, opposite of Q = J → FJ.

NOTE

• Opposite letter pairs add up to 27 (A↔Z, B↔Y ...). Very common in SSC cluster analogies.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(NS, PU, UZ)

(DG, FI, KN)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (RN, TP, YU).

GIVEN

• (NS, PU, UZ) and (DG, FI, KN)

SOLUTION

• Look at the FIRST letters of each set: N(14), P(16), U(21) → gaps +2, +5. Also D(4), F(6), K(11) → gaps +2, +5.

• SECOND letters follow the same +2, +5: S,U,Z and G,I,N.

• Check option 1 (RN, TP, YU): first letters R(18), T(20), Y(25) → +2, +5; second letters N(14), P(16), U(21) → +2, +5. ✓

• Options 2, 3, 4 all give gaps +2, +2 → rejected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The signature is jump pattern +2 then +5 across the three clusters (both letters).

NOTE

• For 'odd set out' cluster questions, compare the position gaps BETWEEN clusters, not just inside a cluster.

question: How many days are there from 2 October 2023 to 9 July 2024 (both inclusive)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 282.

GIVEN

• From 2 October 2023 to 9 July 2024, both days included.

SOLUTION

• Oct (2 to 31) = 30, Nov = 30, Dec = 31, Jan = 31, Feb 2024 (leap) = 29, Mar = 31, Apr = 30, May = 31, Jun = 30, Jul (1 to 9) = 9.

• Total = 30+30+31+31+29+31+30+31+30+9 = 282.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Count remaining days of the start month (31-2+1 = 30), add full months, then the days into the last month (9).

NOTE

• 2024 is a leap year, so February has 29 days — always check leap years in date-counting questions.

question: In the year 1931, which of the following month had 5 Saturdays?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. January.

GIVEN

• Year 1931; find the month with 5 Saturdays.

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 1900 was Monday. From 1900 to 1931 there are 31 years with 7 leap years → odd days = 31+7 = 38 = 3 (mod 7). So 1 Jan 1931 = Monday+3 = Thursday.

• January has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 extra days. The extra days are Thu(1), Fri(2), Sat(3).

• So Thursday, Friday and Saturday each occur 5 times → January has 5 Saturdays.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• A 31-day month gives 5 of its first 3 weekdays. 1 Jan 1931 = Thursday → Thu, Fri, Sat come 5 times.

NOTE

• Odd-days method: only the remainder (mod 7) of total days decides the weekday shift.

question: 5 boys G, H, J, K and L are sitting in a row facing south (not necessarily in the same order). G is to the immediate right of K. H is to the immediate left of J. L is in the middle of the row. H is to the left of L. How many boys are sitting between G and J?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• 5 boys facing SOUTH. G immediate right of K; H immediate left of J; L in the middle; H is to the left of L.

SOLUTION

• Facing south, left = east, right = west. Take positions 1–5 (west→east). L is middle → position 3.

• H is to the left (east) of L and immediate left of J, so J and H sit as J,H at the east end → H = 5, J = 4.

• G immediate right (west) of K gives order G,K → G = 1, K = 2.

• Final row (west→east): G(1), K(2), L(3), J(4), H(5).

• Between G(1) and J(4) sit K and L = 2 boys.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For south-facing rows, swap left↔right, then place the 'middle' person first and build outward.

NOTE

• Facing north: right = east; facing south: right = west. Always flip directions before solving.

question: 7 girls P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). P is the immediate neighbour of Q and R. S is not the immediate neighbour of R or T. V is the immediate neighbour of T and U. V is second to the right of S. Who are the immediate neighbours of S?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Q and U.

GIVEN

• 7 girls around a circle facing centre. P between Q and R; V between T and U; S not adjacent to R or T; V is 2nd to the right of S.

SOLUTION

• Blocks: Q–P–R and T–V–U. S must avoid R and T.

• Place clockwise: R–P–Q–S–U–V–T (and T joins back to R).

• Check: S's neighbours are Q and U (neither R nor T ✓); moving from S, two seats (S→U→V) reach V, so V is 2nd from S ✓.

• Hence immediate neighbours of S = Q and U.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix the two given pairs as blocks, then slot S so it touches neither R nor T — only Q and U remain.

NOTE

• Facing the centre, a person's right is the anticlockwise... test both directions; keep the seating that satisfies every clue.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the second figure.

GIVEN

• First pair: a single-armed 'comb' becomes a comb with an extra lower arm (one more horizontal line is added on the right of the vertical stem).

SOLUTION

• Relation: to the base figure, one extra short horizontal arm is added on the right of the vertical line (the stem gains one more 'tooth').

• Apply the same rule to the third figure → its stem should gain one additional arm in the same manner.

• The figure matching this transformed shape is Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Compare left pair, note the exact change (one arm added), then apply that single change to the third figure.

NOTE

• In figure analogies, isolate ONE consistent transformation (addition, rotation or reflection) and reproduce it.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the first figure.

GIVEN

• Each box has four corner shapes and a central letter; the first→second box shows a fixed rotation of the four corner shapes.

SOLUTION

• Relation: the four corner shapes are rotated by the same amount (positions cycle) while the central letter changes to the next in sequence.

• Apply the identical rotation of corner shapes to the third box.

• The resulting arrangement matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Track only ONE corner shape from box 1 to box 2 to find the rotation direction, then rotate the third box the same way.

NOTE

• Ignore the central letter for the shape logic — it usually just marks the box; focus on the corner movement.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and third number is related to fourth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

9174 : 9121 :: 1380 : 1327 :: ? : 651
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 704.

GIVEN

• 9174 : 9121 :: 1380 : 1327 :: ? : 651

SOLUTION

• 9174 - 9121 = 53 and 1380 - 1327 = 53. So the first number = second number + 53.

• Required 5th number = 6th number + 53 = 651 + 53 = 704.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The constant gap is +53; add it to 651 → 704.

NOTE

• Whole-number analogies: test the simplest link first (difference or ratio) before anything complex.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

703 : 1177 :: ? : 735 :: 518 : 992
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 261.

GIVEN

• 703 : 1177 :: ? : 735 :: 518 : 992

SOLUTION

• 1177 - 703 = 474 and 992 - 518 = 474. So second number = first number + 474.

• For the middle pair: 735 = ? + 474 → ? = 735 - 474 = 261.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Constant gap +474; subtract from the known second term: 735 - 474 = 261.

NOTE

• When the second term is given, work backwards: first = second - (common difference).

question: In a certain code language, 'ships sailing across river' is coded as 'gel gah gbi gar' and 'river provides easy access' is coded as 'gmq gbi gqm qzs'. How will 'river' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. gbi.

GIVEN

• 'ships sailing across river' = 'gel gah gbi gar'

• 'river provides easy access' = 'gmq gbi gqm qzs'

SOLUTION

• The only common word in the two sentences is 'river'.

• The only common code in the two code sets is 'gbi'.

• Therefore 'river' = gbi.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Match the common WORD with the common CODE across both statements.

NOTE

• Standard 'common word ↔ common code' technique for message-coding problems.

question: In a certain code language, 'OFFER' is coded as '86' and 'LETTER' is coded as '83'. How will 'PASS' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 54.

GIVEN

• OFFER = 86, LETTER = 83.

SOLUTION

• Use reverse alphabet values (A=26, Z=1), i.e. value = 27 - position.

• OFFER = 12+21+21+22+9 = 85, then 85 + 1 = 86 ✓.

• LETTER = 15+22+7+7+22+9 = 82, then 82 + 1 = 83 ✓. So code = (reverse-sum) + 1.

• PASS = 11+26+8+8 = 53, then 53 + 1 = 54.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add reverse-alphabet values of the letters and add 1.

NOTE

• Reverse value of a letter = 27 - (its normal position). Handy for many SSC coding sums.

question: At what time (in PM), the angle between hour and minute hands of a clock will be 27.5 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 12:05.

GIVEN

• Angle between hour and minute hands = 27.5°.

SOLUTION

• Angle formula = |30H − 5.5M|.

• At 12:05 → H = 12 (treated as 0), M = 5: |30(0) − 5.5(5)| = |−27.5| = 27.5° ✓.

• Check others: 1:10 → 25°, 2:15 → 22.5°, 3:20 → 20°. Only 12:05 gives 27.5°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Plug each option into |30H − 5.5M| and pick the one equal to 27.5.

NOTE

• The minute hand moves 5.5° per minute relative to the hour hand; hence the 5.5M term.

question: A clock is 2 minutes slow at 1:15 PM and 6 minutes fast at 7:15 PM. At what time (in PM) will it show the correct time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2:45.

GIVEN

• At 1:15 PM clock is 2 min slow (−2); at 7:15 PM it is 6 min fast (+6).

SOLUTION

• From 1:15 PM to 7:15 PM = 6 hours = 360 minutes.

• Total gain = from −2 to +6 = 8 minutes over 360 minutes.

• To reach correct time it must gain 2 minutes (from −2 to 0): time = (2/8) × 360 = 90 minutes.

• 1:15 PM + 90 minutes = 2:45 PM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Gain rate = 8 min per 360 min. Need +2 min ⇒ (2/8)×360 = 90 min after 1:15 → 2:45.

NOTE

• The clock gains uniformly; use proportion of the required correction to the total gain.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the third figure.

GIVEN

• A box holds four circles arranged as a diagonal chain (top-left to bottom-right); their internal designs change from figure to figure.

SOLUTION

• Relation: the internal fill-patterns of the four circles shift one position along the chain at every step (the sequence of designs rotates).

• Continuing this shift for the fifth figure gives the arrangement shown in Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Follow one particular fill design as it moves along the diagonal; predict its next seat to pick the answer.

NOTE

• In figure-series, keep the outer frame fixed and track only the moving/shifting internal element.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the first figure.

GIVEN

• Each box shows curved arcs in its corners; from figure to figure one more arc is added to the corners.

SOLUTION

• Relation: at each step an additional small arc appears in the corners, thickening the corner clusters step by step.

• Extending this growth for the fifth figure gives the fully-built corners shown in Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Count the arcs in each corner across the series; the next figure has one more in each corner.

NOTE

• 'Growing/adding element' series: identify what is added each step and extend the count.

question: Difference between the present ages of A and B is 12 years. 5 years ago from present, the ratio of ages of A and B is 5 : 3. What is the present age of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 23 years.

GIVEN

• Present difference of A and B = 12 years; 5 years ago A : B = 5 : 3.

SOLUTION

• Let ages 5 years ago be 5x and 3x. Their difference is the same now: 5x − 3x = 2x = 12 → x = 6.

• B five years ago = 3x = 18 → present B = 18 + 5 = 23 years.

• (Check: A = 5x + 5 = 35; 35 − 23 = 12 ✓.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference of a ratio a:b equals (a−b) parts = given difference. Here 2 parts = 12 → 1 part = 6, then B = 3×6 + 5 = 23.

NOTE

• The age difference between two people never changes with time — use it to find one part of the ratio.

question: Father's age 12 years ago from present was 2 times of the age of his son 3 years ago from present. Son's age after 12 years from present is 28 years. What is present age of father?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 38 years.

GIVEN

• Father 12 years ago = 2 × (son 3 years ago). Son's age after 12 years = 28.

SOLUTION

• Son's present age = 28 − 12 = 16 years.

• Son 3 years ago = 16 − 3 = 13 years.

• Father 12 years ago = 2 × 13 = 26 years.

• Father's present age = 26 + 12 = 38 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Work the son's line first (16 → 13), double it (26), then add back 12 → 38.

NOTE

• Convert every 'ago/after' phrase to present age first, then apply the given relation.
